page.layout: One column of running text, with marginal notes in the left margin. The left margin holds one note, set beside the lines "nobili ad hoc" to "misso". Below the text there is nothing but a catchword at the right.
page.running_head: De Agro Frif. inter Lavic. & Amaf.

main_text.l: ne in Frisiam jus ad eundem transiret. Al-
bertus per suos, quos præmiserat, op-
aversis, inque fidem suam adactis, Gro-
tavit. Nam hos quoque ad imperium sibi
Maximilianum. Verùm cùm res per in-
ipse ob filii casum, quem Translavicani
que negotio agrum in suam potestatem
& fidem redegit. Sed in obsidenda urbe
nobili ad hoc à Principibus Germaniæ
misso, & cum eo Friderico Badensi epi-
coiit, anno M. D. mense Augusto: in quo

page.notes: The marginal note reads "Albertus / Groningā / obsdet." Its last word is hard to read at this scan resolution; the letter after "obs" may be an i, so the reading "obsdet." is doubtful. The last line of the page is "bel-", continued by "lum" at the right, which I have given as the catchword. Greek and Hebrew do not occur on this page. The gray credit line at the bottom right of the scan is the digitiser's mark and is not transcribed.
